question: Under Sub-section (2) of Section 4, how is the tax payable by an individual computed?
expected_answer: By applying the rates mentioned in Schedule-1 to the person's taxable income, after deducting the amount adjustable in tax under Section 51 or 71.

question: Under Sub-section (5) of Section 4, what rate applies to income sent abroad by a foreign permanent establishment?
expected_answer: The rate mentioned in Sub-section (6) of Section 2 of Schedule-1, applied to the income sent abroad by the establishment in that income year.

question: Under Sub-section (6) of Section 4, how is tax computed for a person referred to in clause (c) of Section 3?
expected_answer: By applying the relevant rates to the amount of each payment subject to final tax deduction that the person received in that income year.

question: Which two sections does Sub-section (2) of Section 4 reference for adjusting tax?
expected_answer: Section 51 or Section 71.

question: Under Sub-section (3) of Section 4, what must be true of a resident natural person's employer(s) for their Section 87 tax deduction to be treated as final?
expected_answer: All employers must have become non-resident persons in that income year, and there is only one employer at any one time.

question: Under Sub-section (1) of Section 87, what must a resident employer do with payments sourced in Nepal that are included in computing an employee's income?
expected_answer: Deduct (withhold) tax at the rate referred to in Schedule-1.

question: Under Sub-section (2) of Section 87, if an employer also has a separate right to deduct other amounts from a payment, does that reduce or end their duty to withhold tax?
expected_answer: No — the employer's liability to withhold tax does not decrease or end because of that separate right.

question: Under Section 10, is an amount received under a tax-exemption facility granted by a bilateral or multilateral treaty between Nepal and a foreign country taxable?
expected_answer: No, it is exempted from tax.

question: Under clause (b) of Section 10, what two conditions must be met for a person's foreign-government employment income to be tax-exempt?
expected_answer: The person must be a resident or non-resident solely because of doing that employment, and the amount must be paid from the governmental fund of that foreign country.

question: Under Sub-section (1) of Section 10 of the SSF Act, which scheme addresses protection against unemployment?
expected_answer: The Unemployment protection scheme.

question: Under Section 3 of the SSF Act, can an individual receive social security benefits without contributing to the scheme?
expected_answer: No — an individual who does not contribute to the social security scheme shall not receive social security under the Act.

question: Under Sub-section (4) of Section 5 of the SSF Act, within how many days of the end of the month must a contribution be deposited in the Fund?
expected_answer: Within fifteen days of the end of the month for which the contribution is to be made.

question: Under Section 14 of the SSF Act, if an employer hasn't deposited contributions since an employment relationship began, what must they deposit besides the contribution itself?
expected_answer: The interest applicable as per Section 9, in addition to the contribution owed since the date the employment relationship began.

question: Under Sub-section (1) of Section 7 of the SSF Act, who has the authority to specify the rate of contribution?
expected_answer: The Ministry, by publishing a notice in the Nepal Gazette on the recommendation of the Committee.

question: Under Sub-section (2) of Section 88, what TDS rate applies to a dividend payment made by a resident person?
expected_answer: Ten percent of the total amount of payment.

question: Under Sub-section (2) of Section 51, what percentage of approved medical treatment expenditure forms the basis of the tax adjustment?
expected_answer: Fifteen percent of the approved medical treatment expenditure, plus any amount carried forward under Sub-section (4).

question: Under Sub-section (3) of Section 51, is there a cap on the medical treatment tax adjustment a person can claim in an income year?
expected_answer: Yes — the amount claimed shall not exceed the prescribed limit.

question: Under Sub-section (1) of Section 71, to what extent can a resident person claim adjustment for foreign income tax paid?
expected_answer: To the extent of the tax paid on the assessable foreign income of that person for that year.

question: Under clause (b) of Sub-section (2) of Section 71, can a foreign tax adjustment claim be made at a rate higher than Nepal's average tax rate?
expected_answer: No — the claim cannot be made at a rate of tax higher than the average rate of tax of Nepal payable by that person in that year.

question: Under Sub-section (4) of Section 71, can a person give up their foreign tax adjustment claim and instead claim credit for the foreign income tax?
expected_answer: Yes — Sub-section (4) explicitly allows giving up the adjustment claim and instead claiming credit for foreign income tax, where that facility is available.

question: Under Sub-section (1) of Item 1 of Schedule-1, up to what amount of taxable income is a resident natural person exempt from tax?
expected_answer: Fifty-five Thousand Rupees — no tax is levied on taxable income not exceeding that amount.

question: Under Sub-section (8) of Item 1 of Schedule-1, what tax rate applies to the taxable income of a non-resident natural person?
expected_answer: Twenty-five percent.

question: Under Sub-section (1) of Item 2 of Schedule-1, what is the default tax rate on the taxable income of an entity?
expected_answer: Twenty-five percent, subject to Sub-sections (2), (3), (4), (5) and (7) of that Item.

question: Under Sub-section (2) of Item 2 of Schedule-1, what tax rate applies to a bank, financial institution, or an entity carrying on general insurance business?
expected_answer: Thirty percent.

question: Under clause (ap) of Section 2, what does "Person" mean under the Act?
expected_answer: A natural person or entity.
